statement: The supplied source contains no derivation (including any derivation via logarithm_solve). By definition, a sigmoid function is a bounded, differentiable, real function that is defined for all real input values and has a positive derivative at each point, commonly exemplified by the standard logistic function f(x) = 1 / (1 + e^{-x}).

properties.property: A sigmoid function is monotonic and has a first derivative that is bell-shaped.
properties.why: It is defined to have a strictly positive derivative at every point across the real line.

properties.property: A sigmoid function is constrained by a pair of horizontal asymptotes as x -> ±∞.
properties.why: It is a bounded real function defined for all real inputs, commonly bounded between 0 and 1 or -1 and 1.

properties.property: A sigmoid function is convex for values below an inflection point and concave for values above it.
properties.why: The rate of change rises to a peak and subsequently falls as it approaches the asymptotes.

properties.property: The logistic sigmoid function is invertible, with the logit function as its inverse.
properties.why: It is strictly monotonically increasing on the real domain.

assumptions.assumption: The domain is defined for all real input values x ∈ ℝ.
assumptions.breaks_when: The function is evaluated outside the real numbers or at singularities.

assumptions.assumption: The function is differentiable with a positive derivative at each point.
assumptions.breaks_when: Discontinuous step functions (such as the Heaviside step function) or non-smooth hard sigmoids are used.

failure_modes.mode: Loss of true sigmoidal transition via multiple inflection points
failure_modes.signature: Function exhibits oscillatory behavior or non-monotonic transitions rather than a single inflection point.
failure_modes.cause: Free parameters set outside required bounds in parameterized forms (such as m < √3 in the smooth transition function) or using unitary sigmoids of the 2nd or 3rd kind.

failure_modes.signature: First derivative approaches zero as |x| becomes large.
failure_modes.cause: Inputs x -> ±∞ driving the function into its horizontal asymptotic limits.
